analysis.summary: The PR contains critical infrastructure and code-level bugs, including missing imports that will cause deployment failures, malformed Lambda response structures, and broken SPA routing logic.

bugs.title: ReferenceError: cleanupEnvironment is not defined
bugs.description: The function `cleanupEnvironment` is used in several API route definitions (e.g., lines 127 and 183) but is not imported or defined within the file.
bugs.risk: This will cause an immediate failure during the infrastructure deployment process (e.g., `sst deploy`), preventing any changes from being applied.

bugs.title: Malformed Lambda proxy response due to non-stringified body
bugs.description: The `bffErrorHandling` function returns the raw `error` object as the `body`. AWS Lambda proxy integration requires the `body` field to be a stringified JSON.
bugs.risk: API Gateway will fail to parse the response if `error` is an object (like an AxiosError), resulting in a 500 'Internal Server Error' and preventing the client from receiving the intended error details.

bugs.title: Broken SPA routing/static file resolution
bugs.description: The CloudFront Function (`cfFunction`) responsible for rewriting URIs (appending `.html` and `index.html`) was removed from the S3 behaviors but not replaced by the new Edge Lambda for the specific app path behavior.
bugs.risk: Direct navigation to sub-routes or page refreshes will result in 403 Access Denied or 404 Not Found errors from S3, as CloudFront no longer maps these URIs to the corresponding static assets.

notBugs.reason: The change from '=== false' to '=== true' for the preview parameter is an intended fix for previously counter-intuitive logic.
This is a consistent update; the BFF routes in BffApi.ts now include the full prefixed paths, so stripping them in the dev server proxy is no longer required.
While mutating the error object via `delete error.config` is generally avoided, it is performed here at the end of the request lifecycle to redact sensitive information before logging.
